title: 1981 AHSME Problem 14
statement: In a geometric sequence of real numbers, the sum of the first two terms is \(7,\) and the sum of the first six terms is \(91.\) The sum of the first four terms is

solutions.text:
If the first term is \(a\) and ratio is \(r,\) then \[ 91=a(1+r)(1+r^2+r^4). \] Since \(a(1+r)=7,\) we have \(1+r^2+r^4=13.\) With \(t=r^2\ge0,\) \(t^2+t-12=0,\) so \(t=3.\) The first four terms sum to \(a(1+r)(1+r^2)=7(4)=28.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Factor the first-six-term sum into the first-two-term sum times \(1+r^2+r^4\)
